name: 1 John
sourceNote: Translated from the Greek text of B. F. Westcott and F. J. A. Hort, *The New Testament in the Original Greek* (1881; public domain), with Tischendorf’s eighth edition (1869–72; public domain) consulted. Variant readings were also compared with the SBL Greek New Testament, the Nestle–Aland *Novum Testamentum Graece*, and the Byzantine text of Robinson and Pierpont, which were consulted for variants only. Where manuscript readings are cited in the notes, they are reported from the standard editions and have not been verified against the manuscripts. Greek *kyrios* is rendered “Lord”; where an Old Testament passage with the divine name is quoted or echoed, a note gives the Hebrew *Yahweh*. *Christos* is rendered “Christ” where it functions as part of Jesus’ name. The letter names no author. Early tradition (Irenaeus, late 2nd century) ascribes it, with the Gospel of John, to John the apostle; many scholars regard it as the work of a leader in the same circle of churches, and this translation takes no position. Its language closely resembles that of John’s Gospel. The chief early witnesses are Codices Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and Vaticanus. The “Johannine Comma,” a Trinitarian addition at 5:7–8 found in the King James Version, is not part of the Greek text followed here; see the note at 5:7.

verses.text: What existed from the beginning, what we have heard, what our own eyes have seen, what we gazed on and our hands handled, concerning the word of life:{a}
The life was disclosed; we have seen it, we testify to it, and we report to you that eternal life which was in the Father’s presence and was disclosed to us.
We announce to you also what we have seen and heard, so that you too may have a common life with us; and our common life is with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ.{b}
We write this so that the joy we share may be full.{c}
This is the message we have heard from him and pass on to you: God is light, and in him there is no darkness whatever.
If we claim to have fellowship with him while we walk in the darkness, we are lying and are not living out the truth.
But if we walk in the light as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus his Son cleanses us from all sin.{d}
If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and there is no truth within us.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just, so that he forgives us our sins and cleanses us from all wrongdoing.
If we say we have never sinned, we make him out to be a liar, and his message is not in us.

notes.text: Word of life: Greek *logos*, “word,” “message”; compare John 1:1–4.
Fellowship: Greek *koinōnia*, “sharing,” “partnership.”
The joy we share: literally “our joy”; many manuscripts read “your joy.” *We write*: later manuscripts read “we write to you.”
Jesus: later manuscripts read “Jesus Christ.”

verses.text: My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you may not sin. But if anyone does sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous one.{a}
He himself is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not for ours alone but also for those of the whole world.{b}
And by this we can be sure that we have come to know him: if we keep his commandments.
Anyone who claims, “I know him,” yet ignores what he commands is lying, and the truth has no place in such a person.
Whoever keeps to his word, though, is someone in whom God’s love has truly reached its goal. This is how we can tell we are in him:
whoever says he remains in him ought himself to walk as that one walked.{c}
Dear friends, it is no new commandment I am writing to you, but an old commandment, which you have had from the beginning. The old commandment is the word you have heard.{d}
Yet I am writing to you a new commandment, which is true in him and in you, because the darkness is passing away and the true light is already shining.
Whoever says he is in the light but hates his brother is still in the darkness.{e}
Whoever loves his brother remains in the light, and there is nothing in him to make him stumble.
But whoever hates his brother is in the darkness and walks in the darkness, and does not know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes.

I am writing to you, little children,
because your sins have been forgiven for his name’s sake.

I am writing to you, fathers,
because you know him who is from the beginning.
I am writing to you, young men,
because you have overcome the evil one.
I have written to you, children,
because you know the Father.{f}

I have written to you, fathers,
because you know him who is from the beginning.
I have written to you, young men,
because you are strong,
and the word of God remains in you,
and you have overcome the evil one.{g}
Do not love the world or the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him.
For everything in the world, the craving of the flesh and the craving of the eyes and the arrogance of life, is not from the Father but from the world.{h}
And the world is passing away, and its craving, but whoever does the will of God remains forever.{i}
Children, it is the last hour; and as you heard that antichrist is coming, so now many antichrists have arisen. That is how we know that it is the last hour.{j}
They went out from us, but they did not belong to us; for if they had belonged to us, they would have stayed with us. But they went out so that it might be made plain that none of them belong to us.
But you have an anointing from the Holy One, and you all know.{k}
My reason for writing is not that the truth is unknown to you, but that you know it, and that no falsehood has its source in the truth.
Who is a liar if not the one who says Jesus is not the Christ? Such a person, disowning both Father and Son, is the antichrist.
No one who denies the Son has the Father either; whoever confesses the Son has the Father too.{l}
Let the message you heard from the beginning stay in you. If it stays in you, you also will stay in the Son and in the Father.{m}
And the promise he has given us is this: life eternal.
What I have written here concerns those who would mislead you.

But you have the anointing you received from him remaining in you, and so you need no one to instruct you. His anointing instructs you in all things; it is genuine and no falsehood. So, as it has instructed you, remain in him.{n}
And now, my little ones, remain in him, so that when he is revealed we may stand unafraid and not turn from him ashamed when he comes.{o}
Since you know that he is just, be sure of this too: every person who practices justice is his offspring.

notes.text: Advocate: Greek *paraklētos*, “one called alongside,” “helper,” the word used of the Spirit in John 14:16.
Atoning sacrifice: Greek *hilasmos*, “means of atonement,” “propitiation,” “expiation.”
Remains: Greek *menein*, “remain,” “remain,” “dwell,” a key word of this letter.
Dear friends: literally “beloved ones.” Later manuscripts read “Brothers.” *You have heard*: later manuscripts add “from the beginning.”
Brother: that is, a fellow believer, whether brother or sister; so throughout the letter.
I have written: some manuscripts read “I am writing.” In verses 13–14 the verb changes from present to past tense, perhaps for variety, perhaps referring to this letter or an earlier one.
Of God: Westcott and Hort bracket these words.
Arrogance of life: or “pride in possessions”; Greek *bios* can mean “life” or “livelihood.”
Its craving: Westcott and Hort bracket “its.”
Antichrist: Greek *antichristos*, “opponent of Christ” or “one in place of Christ”; in the New Testament the word occurs only in 1 and 2 John.
You all know: many manuscripts read “you know all things.” *Anointing*: Greek *chrisma*, related to *Christos*, “anointed one.”
Whoever confesses the Son has the Father too: later manuscripts omit this sentence.
In the Father: Westcott and Hort bracket “in.”
Remain in him: or “you remain in him.”
Comes: Greek *parousia*, “arrival,” “presence.”

verses.text: Look how great a love the Father has lavished on us, that we are named God’s children; and that is what we are! The world fails to recognize us for this reason: it failed to recognize him.{a}
Beloved, we are God’s children now, and what we will become has not yet been made clear. We do know that when he is revealed we will be like him, because we will see him just as he is.{b}
And everyone who has this hope set on him purifies himself, as he is pure.
Everyone who commits sin also commits lawlessness; sin is lawlessness.
You know that he appeared in order to take away sins, and in him there is no sin.{c}
Whoever remains in him does not go on in sin; whoever goes on in sin has neither seen nor known him.
Little children, let no one lead you astray. Whoever does what is right is righteous, just as he is righteous.
The one who keeps on sinning belongs to the devil, since the devil has sinned from the start. The Son of God appeared for this reason: to demolish the devil’s work.{d}
A person begotten by God does not practice sin, since God’s seed remains in him; indeed he is unable to go on sinning, since God is his father.{e}
Here is what shows who are God’s children and who are the devil’s: anyone who fails to practice justice is not God’s, and the same is true of anyone who fails to love his brother.
For this is the message you have heard from the beginning, that we should love one another,
Do not be like Cain, who came from the evil one and cut his brother’s throat. Why did he kill him? Because what he did was wicked, while what his brother did was upright.{f}
Do not be surprised, brothers, if the world hates you.{g}
We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brothers. Whoever does not love remains in death.{h}
Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life remaining in him.
By this we have come to know love, that he laid down his life for us; and we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers.
Whoever has this world’s means of life and notices a brother in want, yet shuts off his compassion from him, how can God’s love be remaining in such a one?{i}
Little children, let us love not in word or with the tongue but in deed and in truth.
This is how we will know that we belong to the truth, and we will set our hearts at rest in his presence{j}
whenever our heart condemns us, because God is greater than our heart, and he knows everything.
Dear friends, if our heart does not condemn us, we have confidence before God,
and whatever we ask we receive from him, because we keep his commandments and do what pleases him.
And this is his commandment, that we should believe in the name of his Son Jesus Christ and love one another, just as he commanded us.
The one who obeys what God commands remains in God, and God in that person. And here is how we know he remains in us: by the Spirit he gave us.

notes.text: That is what we are: later manuscripts omit these words.
When he appears: or “when it is revealed.”
Sins: later manuscripts read “our sins.”
Devil: Greek *diabolos*, “slanderer.”
God’s seed: literally “his seed”; perhaps God’s nature or his word.
Gen 4:1–16. *Cain*: perhaps “acquired” (Gen 4:1), or “smith.”
Brothers: Greek *adelphoi*, which includes sisters.
Whoever does not love: later manuscripts add “his brother.”
Compassion: literally “inward parts.”
Reassure: or “persuade.” *Our hearts*: literally “our heart”; so in verses 20–21.

verses.text: Dear friends, do not trust every spirit; put the spirits to the test, whether they come from God, since many false prophets have gone forth into the world.
By this you know the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses Jesus Christ as having come in the flesh is from God,
But any spirit that refuses to confess Jesus does not come from God. That spirit belongs to the antichrist; you were told it was on its way, and already it is here in the world.{a}
You, little ones, come from God, and you have defeated them, since the one in you is mightier than the one in the world.
Those people belong to the world, so the world is the source of their talk, and the world gives them a hearing.
We come from God. Anyone who knows God gives us a hearing; anyone not from God gives us none. That is how we tell the Spirit of truth from the spirit of deception.
Beloved, let us love each other, for love comes from God, and all who love are God’s children and know God.
Whoever does not love has not known God, because God is love.
God’s love became visible among us like this: God sent his only Son into the world so that we could have life through him.{b}
Love consists in this: not that we have loved God, but that he loved us and sent his Son as the sacrifice that covers our sins.{c}
Dear friends, if God so loved us, we also ought to love one another.
God no one has ever beheld; yet if we love one another, God remains in us and his love has reached its goal in us.
By this we know that we remain in him and he in us, because he has given us of his Spirit.
And we have seen and testify that the Father has sent the Son as Savior of the world.
Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God remains in him, and he in God.{d}
And we ourselves have come to know the love God has for us, and we have put our trust in it. God is love; whoever remains in love remains in God, and God remains in that person.{e}
By this love is brought to completion with us, so that we may have confidence on the day of judgment, because as he is, so also are we in this world.
Fear has no place in love; rather, love that is complete drives fear out, for fear has to do with punishment, and one who is afraid has not yet been made complete in love.
We love, because he first loved us.{f}
If anyone says, “I love God,” and hates his brother, he is a liar; for whoever does not love his brother whom he has seen cannot love God whom he has not seen.{g}
And this commandment we have from him: whoever loves God must love his brother also.

notes.text: Refuses to confess Jesus: later manuscripts read “does not confess that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh.” Some early witnesses, as reported, read “sets Jesus aside” or “dissolves Jesus” (Greek *lyei*).
Unique: Greek *monogenēs*, “one and only,” “only.”
Atoning sacrifice: Greek *hilasmos*; see 2:2.
Jesus: Westcott and Hort bracket “Christ” after “Jesus.”
For us: literally “in us.” *Remains in that person*: Westcott and Hort bracket the second “remains.”
We love: later manuscripts read “We love him.”
Cannot: some manuscripts read “how can he?”

verses.text: All who believe Jesus to be the Christ are God’s offspring, and everyone who loves the father loves his child as well.
By this we know that we love the children of God, when we love God and carry out his commandments.{a}
For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments; and his commandments are not burdensome.
For everything born of God overcomes the world, and this is the victory that has overcome the world: our faith.
Who conquers the world? Only the person who believes Jesus is God’s Son.{b}
This is the one who came by water and blood, Jesus Christ; not by water alone, but by water and by blood. And the Spirit is the witness, because the Spirit is truth.{c}
For there are three that testify:{d}
the Spirit, the water and the blood; and the three are in agreement.{e}
If we accept human testimony, the testimony of God is greater; for this is the testimony of God, that he has testified concerning his Son.
Those who believe in God’s Son carry the witness within themselves. Those who refuse to believe God have called him a liar, since they have not trusted the witness God has given about his Son.{f}
And this is the witness: God gave us eternal life, and that life is found in his Son.
To have the Son is to have life; not to have God’s Son is to be without life.
I have written these things to you so that you may know that you have eternal life, you who believe in the name of the Son of God.{g}
We have this boldness in approaching him: whenever we ask for anything in line with his will, he listens to us.
And if we know that he hears us in whatever we ask, we know that we have the requests we have asked of him.

If anyone sees his brother committing a sin not leading to death, he shall ask, and God will give him life, for those who sin not to death. There is sin that leads to death; I do not say that one should pray about that.
Every wrong is sin, but not all sin is deadly.
We know that everyone born of God does not keep on sinning, but the one born of God guards him, and the evil one does not touch him.{h}
We know that we are of God, and the whole world lies in the power of the evil one.
We know too that the Son of God has come and given us insight to know the true one; and we are in the true one, in his Son Jesus Christ. He is the true God and eternal life.{i}
Little children, keep yourselves from idols.{j}

notes.text: Carry out: later manuscripts read “keep.”
Who is it: Westcott and Hort bracket a Greek particle, “and” or “but,” after “who.”
Water and blood: perhaps Jesus’ baptism and death; compare John 19:34. Some manuscripts read “water and spirit,” or “water and blood and spirit.”

Later Latin manuscripts and a few late Greek manuscripts add, in verses 7–8, “in heaven, the Father, the Word and the Holy Spirit, and these three are one; and there are three that testify on earth.” This addition, the “Johannine Comma,” appears in no Greek manuscript before the 14th century except as a later marginal note, as reported in the standard editions; it entered printed Greek texts in Erasmus’s third edition (1522) and so passed into the King James Version. It is not part of the text followed here.
Are in agreement: literally “are into the one.”
In himself: some manuscripts read “in him.” *Believe God*: some manuscripts read “believe the Son.”
Later manuscripts add “and that you may believe in the name of the Son of God.”
The one born of God: that is, the Son of God. *Guards him*: many manuscripts read “guards himself.”
He is the true God: “He” may refer to the Father or to Jesus Christ.
Later manuscripts add “Amen.”
